lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.25 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details: Listen and say checks understanding of word meaning and pronunciation of the verbs. Then practise allows students to produce the ‘I’ and ‘you’ forms of the present continuous through a structured question and answer sequence.
Look for careful listening and correct pronunciation of each verb, correct production of the grammar structure, particularly the -ing form, and authentic intonation.
“Hurray - today, our friends want to play outside with us. What shall we do?

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.25 - B. Ask and answer

details: Ask and Answer gives students controlled practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions, in this case the ‘he’ and ‘she’ forms of the present continuous.
Look for correct formation of the question form, particularly the -ing form, correct pronunciation and authentic intonation in both the question and the answer.
“We’ve come to the park! What can we do here? Let’s see what everyone else is doing!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.81 - A Look and match

details: Look and match practises word recognition and word-concept association
Look for accurate choices and neat lines in the students’ books.
“That was so much fun. I’d like to write in my diary about what we did.  Can you help me match the words to the pictures so I remember?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.81 - B Look and write

details: Look and write tests students’ written production of the infinitives identified in the word search and the -ing forms.
Look for correct formation of the -ing forms, correct spelling of both forms, neat handwriting between the lines.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.26 - Speaking Guess the Action

details: The Guess the Action speaking activity provides freer oral production practice of the grammar structure, further consolidating the present continuous question and answer structures (in the ‘I’ and ‘you’ forms).
Look for correct question and answer structures, correct pronunciation, authentic intonation and active participation.
“We don’t even need to be outside to do all these activities. Let’s have a go doing them inside!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (closed pairs): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (open pairs): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs
As well as being fun, the song gives students the chance to practise the natural rhythms and intonation of the language in an authentic context.
Look for active participation from all students, correct pronunciation and authentic intonation.
“Wow, I’m tired now with all this dancing, running and jumping! But before we finish, let’s do one more thing – let’s sing a song!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.

Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video Song):
